Subject: The Beacon headlamp: 400 lumens, 40 hours, 95 grams
Preview: Charge it at the trailhead. Use it for the whole trip.
Body: You know how a headlamp can quietly make or break a trip — the predawn start, the longer-than-expected descent, the camp chores after dark.

The Northbay Beacon is built around three numbers worth knowing before you pack it.

**400 lumens.** Enough output to read the trail ahead at a solid pace or light up a campsite without fumbling for a lantern.

**40 hours of runtime.** On a single charge, that covers a long weekend with room to spare. You won't be rationing light on night two.

**95 grams.** It sits on your head, not on your neck. Noticeable over a full day; easy to forget about during a night run.

**USB-C rechargeable.** Same cable as your phone, your battery pack, your headphones. One fewer thing to think about at the trailhead.

A note on limits: the Beacon is a trail and camp headlamp. It's not rated for technical caving or dive use. It does exactly what a three-season backpacker needs it to do — reliably, trip after trip.

The Beacon is available now.
